description: 2012 is the Year of the Water Dragon in the Chinese zodiac, from January 23, 2012 to February 9, 2013. Personality, Lunar New Year dates and numerology.
answer: In Chinese astrology, 2012 is the Year of the Water Dragon, a Yang year. It began at Lunar New Year on January 23, 2012 and ended on February 9, 2013, so people born in 2012 before Jan 23 belong to the Metal Rabbit year.

sections.heading: 2012 Lunar New Year: start and end dates
paragraphs: Lunar New Year opened the Water Dragon year on January 23, 2012, and the year ran to February 9, 2013. So a birth date of Jan 23, 2012 or later counts as Water Dragon, and so do early 2013 birthdays through Feb 9; births in 2012 before Jan 23 still belong to the Metal Rabbit. That moving boundary comes from the lunisolar calendar, in which the new year starts with the second new moon after the winter solstice in most years, so its Gregorian date shifts by up to a month from one year to the next. Look sixty years either side and the pairing repeats: 1952 are Water Dragon years too. That Monday new year arrived with the Sun in Aquarius in the Western zodiac.

sections.heading: What the Water Dragon is like
paragraphs: Picture a Dragon that wins through perception rather than force. With Earth shaping Water, those born in this year are described as composed, adaptable and quietly influential, gifted at mediation and long-range planning. Their steadiness reassures others. Readings suggest showing unguarded feelings more often and acting on instinct before perfect certainty arrives. Their influence tends to be felt long before it is noticed, and it is usually used with considerable care.

In classical thought, Water belongs to the north and to the deep, resting energy of winter, the season when life gathers strength out of sight. As a year stem, it tends to make an animal more reflective, adaptable and emotionally attuned. People born under a Water stem are often described as clever negotiators, sensitive friends and natural mediators who prefer influence to force. They value understanding and tend to think before they act. The caution traditionally attached to Water is fluidity taken too far: avoiding conflict, keeping too much hidden and losing a clear sense of their own direction.

sections.heading: 2012 in the animal cycle and in numerology
paragraphs: In numerology the year reduces to 5, the number of change, freedom and movement, and a 5 year is usually described as restless and full of variety. The digits of 2012 add up to 5. The Dragon holds the fifth place among the twelve animals and its fixed element is Earth. Set beside the year's Water stem, earth controls Water, which readings use to describe how settled or stretched the combination feels. The year before was the Metal Rabbit and the year after is the Water Snake.

Chinese almanacs name 2012 Ren-Chen, pairing the Water stem Ren with the branch Chen. Both are Yang, as stem and branch always share a polarity, so of the hundred and twenty possible pairings only sixty ever occur, and each one names a single year in every cycle.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac is 2012?
faq.answer: 2012 is the Year of the Water Dragon. It started on January 23, 2012 and ended on February 9, 2013.

faq.question: What if I was born in January or February 2012?
faq.answer: Check the date against Jan 23. Born before January 23, 2012, you are a Metal Rabbit; born on or after it, you are a Water Dragon.

faq.question: What element is 2012 in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Water, a Yang year. The Dragon's own fixed element is Earth; the year element changes every two years, while the fixed element stays with the animal.

faq.question: What is the traditional Chinese name for 2012?
faq.answer: Ren-Chen. The first part is the heavenly stem, which carries the year's element and polarity; the second is the earthly branch, which carries the animal. Almanacs, calendars and Four Pillars charts identify years this way rather than by animal alone.

faq.question: When is the next Water Dragon year?
faq.answer: 2072, sixty years later, when the five elements and twelve animals line up again; the table also has 1952.
